newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end sharply off but Intel buoys techs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end sharply off but Intel buoys techs.

text.p: U.S. stocks were battered for the second time in less than a week as a flurry of unsubstantiated rumors slammed into an already nervous market and bond yields pressed higher.

The Dow industrials lost 71 points or 1.09 percent to about 6403 after falling nearly 130 points earlier. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite shed only three to about 1309 as bellwether Intel rallied 7-3/4 to 136-7/8.
"The tape looked bad this morning, like the world was coming to an end," said James Cramer, president of Cramer Co.

Alexander & Alexander Services rose three to 17-1/8 and AON Corp added 1-1/4 to 58-7/8. AON agreed to acquire Alexander & Alexander for $17.50 cash per common share plus considerations for preferred shares.
As for overall stocks near term, Ducey did not see Wednesday's selling as the start of the long-awaited 10 percent correction. "We'll soon be moving into year-end window-dressing," he said.
But he also noted that Friday the 13th is coming up.
